title: Hopf dimension inequality for a bilinear map without zero divisors
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $V,W,T$ be finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] with $V
e0$ and $W
e0$. Let $b:V	imes W	o T$ be $k$-bilinear, meaning linear in each argument. Suppose $b(v,w)
e0$ whenever $v
e0$ and $w
e0$. Let $P\subseteq T$ be the linear span of all $b(v,w)$, namely their finite $k$-linear combinations. Then
$$\dim_kP\geq\dim_kV+\dim_kW-1.$$
In particular $\dim_kT\geq\dim_kV+\dim_kW-1$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary for the Clifford argument underlying Section 3.2, step (7), printed p.14 (Morrison only lists that step, rather than proving this linear algebra lemma). Hopf inequality reconstructed via the Segre variety and linear sections; complete argument retained in report.md. Local Morrison PDF WANTED; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340.

proof.text: Put $m=\dim_kV\geq1$, $n=\dim_kW\geq1$, $p=\dim_kP$ and choose bases $v_i,w_j$. The coordinate space $E=k^{m n}$ has its coordinate basis $e_{ij}$. Define $B:E\to P$ by $B(e_{ij})=b(v_i,w_j)$. Bilinearity gives $b(\sum_i a_iv_i,\sum_j c_jw_j)=\sum_{ij}a_ic_jb(v_i,w_j)$, so the image of $B$ is precisely $P$. For $K=\ker B$ and $d=\dim_kK$, [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] gives $p+d=mn$. The finite-dimensional hypotheses hold for $E$ by its coordinate basis and for $P$ because the $mn$ vectors $b(v_i,w_j)$ span it.

source.place: Agent coordinate linearization and rank-nullity, preparatory to the application of Tag 0B2R.

proof.text: In $\mathbf P(E)=\mathbf P^{mn-1}_k$, use [def-chow-segre] and [lem-chow-segre] to form the nonempty closed Segre image $X$ of $\mathbf P^{m-1}_k\times_k\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$, with coordinates $z_{ij}=a_ic_j$. If $d>0$, let $L$ be the common zero locus of the homogeneous linear coordinate functions of $B$. Choose a basis of $K$ and extend it to a basis of $E$. In these coordinates the equations of $L$ set the last $mn-d$ coordinates to zero, so $L$ is a closed copy of $\mathbf P^{d-1}_k$. The coordinate change is an isomorphism: an invertible matrix and its inverse act on homogeneous coordinates; on an open where a transformed coordinate is nonzero, the ratios of the transformed linear forms are regular, and the inverse ratios give the inverse map. The description of a closed immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies $X$ homeomorphically with its source.

source.place: Agent Segre/kernel construction using Constructions Tag 01WD (constructions-lemma-segre-embedding), read in constructions.tex:2926-2986.

proof.text: Here are the dimensions, including projective spaces of dimension zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], $\mathbf P^r_k$ has a cover by $r+1$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], products of such charts have coordinate ring $k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\otimes_k k[u_1,\ldots,u_s]\cong k[t_1,\ldots,t_r,u_1,\ldots,u_s]$: send the two sets of variables to the corresponding tensor factors; the inverse sends a pure tensor $f\otimes g$ to $fg$. These maps are inverse on variables and pure tensors. Since a field has just two ideals, it is Noetherian of ring dimension zero. Thus [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] give dimension $r$ for each single chart and $r+s$ for each product chart.

source.place: Constructions Tag 01NG (constructions-lemma-standard-covering-projective-space); agent polynomial-chart computation of the dimensions used in Tag 0B2R.

proof.text: The scheme spaces in step 3 are sober by [lem-sc-scheme-sober], hence quasi-sober and $T_0$: if two points had the same closure, uniqueness of its generic point would make them equal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-bound-open-cover] to those chart covers for the upper bounds, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] to any nonempty chart for the reverse bounds. Isomorphisms preserve chains of irreducible closed subsets and their lengths. Consequently $\dim X=m+n-2$, and if $d>0$, $\dim L=d-1$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the chart dimensions; the dimensions inserted in varieties-lemma-intersection-in-projective-space (Tag 0B2R).

proof.text: Assume $d>0$. The closed subsets $X$ and $L$ are disjoint. Otherwise [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], applied to the ambient $\mathbf P^{mn-1}_k$, supplies a closed point $x\in X\cap L$: closed points in this nonempty closed subset are dense. The ambient scheme is locally of finite type, since its standard affine charts in step 3 are finite-variable polynomial algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], $\kappa(x)=k$ as a $k$-algebra. The closed immersion onto $X$ lifts this rational point to the Segre source: on affine rings it is a quotient, and a point killing that quotient ideal factors through it, with the same residue field [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The two projections are $k$-points of the factors, so the chart coordinates give nonzero vectors $a\in k^m$ and $c\in k^n$ representing them. By [def-chow-segre], their Segre coordinates are $(a_ic_j)$. Membership in $L$ says $B((a_ic_j))=0$, hence $b(\sum_i a_iv_i,\sum_j c_jw_j)=0$. Both arguments are nonzero by basis independence, contradicting the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0478 (varieties-lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson) and the algebraically closed residue-field consequence; agent disjointness argument.

proof.text: If $d>0$, both $X,L$ are nonempty. The contrapositive of [lem-sfb-projective-closed-intersection-dimension], with ambient dimension $mn-1$, now gives $(m+n-2)+(d-1)<mn-1$. Since these are integers, $m+n+d\leq mn+1$, and $p=mn-d\geq m+n-1$. If $d=0$, step 1 gives $p=mn$; the same bound follows from $mn-(m+n-1)=(m-1)(n-1)\geq0$. This case avoids assigning an ordinary nonnegative dimension to the empty projectivization of the zero space.

source.place: Tag 0B2R (varieties-lemma-intersection-in-projective-space), contrapositive and integer rearrangement; separate zero-kernel case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-vector-space-quotient-dimension] to $P\subseteq T$: $\dim_k(T/P)+\dim_kP=\dim_kT$. Since the quotient dimension is nonnegative, $\dim_kT\geq\dim_kP$. Combine with step 6 to obtain the second asserted bound.

source.place: Elementary consequence of the dimension formula for the subspace P of T.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q70-882619ed8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and the new node in full, every cited statement, and the sources Stacks 0B2R (varieties.tex 6365-6412), 01WD and 0478. Item statement is unchanged and still unsplit on live, so this is a first split with no parallel duplicate and no SGA source. Step 1: rank-nullity applied to B: k^{mn} -> P gives p+d=mn, and the image of B is exactly the span P. Step 2: lem-chow-segre gives the closed Segre image X; L=P(K) becomes a coordinate-linear subspace after an explicit elementary change of coordinates. Steps 3-4: chart, tensor and polynomial-dimension nodes plus the open-cover upper bound and monotone lower bound (sober scheme spaces) give dim X=m+n-2 and dim L=d-1. Step 5: Jacobson density gives a closed point of X∩L with residue field k (algebraic closedness used here); lifting through the closed immersion gives a zero product b(a·v,c·w)=0, a contradiction. Step 6: the contrapositive of the new 0B2R node gives m+n+d-3<mn-1, which is equivalent to p>=m+n-1; the d=0 case is handled separately. New node matches 0B2R hypothesis by hypothesis over any field, is statement-only, and is not a clause of the item; rg -L over snapshot, live and side-live found no duplicate. Small cases checked: m=n=1, m=1, the polynomial product (sharp bound), C×C->C over R (closedness needed), N=0, and skew lines in P^3.
